source.label: thm:high-prob
source.quote: Suppose $K \geq 2$ and $\delta \in (0,1/4)$ and $T \geq 32 (K-1) \log(2/\delta)$, then there exists a sequence of losses $\ell_{1:T} \in [0,1]^{KT}$ such that $\Pr{R_T(\ell_{1:T}) \geq \frac{1}{27} \sqrt{(K-1)T \log(1/(4\delta))}} \geq \delta/2$ ... Furthermore $\ell_{1:T}$ can be chosen in such a way that there exists an $i$ such that for all $t$ it holds that $\ell_{i,t} = \min_j \ell_{j,t}$ and $\max_{j,k} \{\ell_{j,t} - \ell_{k,t}\} \leq \sqrt{(K-1) \log(1/(4\delta))/T}/(4\sqrt{\log 2})$.

results.notes: Regret exceeds the bound with probability at least delta/2 (not 1-delta), i.e. a lower bound on the (1-delta/2)-quantile of regret. The hard sequence also has a uniformly optimal arm and small effective range.

bound.regime: sqrt((K-1)/T) log(1/(4 delta)) <= C, T >= 32 log(2/delta)

symbols.C_exp: constant such that the strategy satisfies E[R_T] <= C sqrt((K-1)T) for all loss sequences

source.label: thm:high-prob-uniform
source.quote: Suppose $K \geq 2$, $T \geq 1$, and there exists a strategy and constant $C > 0$ such that for any $\ell_{1:T} \in [0,1]^{KT}$ it holds that $\E[R_T(\ell_{1:T})] \leq C \sqrt{(K-1)T}$. Let $\delta \in (0,1/4)$ satisfy $\sqrt{(K-1)/T} \log(1/(4\delta)) \leq C$ and $T \geq 32 \log(2/\delta)$. Then there exists $\ell_{1:T} \in [0,1]^{KT}$ for which $\Pr{R_T(\ell_{1:T}) \geq \frac{\sqrt{(K-1)T}\log(1/(4\delta))}{203 C}} \geq \delta / 2$

results.notes: Applies to strategies with minimax-optimal expected regret C sqrt((K-1)T). Probability of exceeding is at least delta/2. Corollary 3 (no strategy has P(R_T >= C sqrt((K-1)T) log^p(1/delta)) <= delta for all delta, p<1) follows; not recorded separately as it is an impossibility statement.

bound.regime: T >= max(K,118), alpha in [max(c log(32T), K/2)/T, 1/2], c = 64/9

symbols.a_ball: radius alpha of the small-loss ball: L*_T/T <= alpha

source.label: thm:firstorder-lowerbound
source.quote: Let $K \geq 2$, $T \geq K \vee 118$, and $\alpha \in \left[(c \log(32 T) \vee (K/2))/T, 1/2\right]$, where $c=64/9$. Then for any randomised bandit algorithm $\sup_{\ell_{1:T} \in \cB_{\alpha,T}} \E[\Reg_T(\ell_{1:T})] \geq \sqrt{\alpha T K} / 27$, where the expectation is taken with respect to the internal randomisation of the algorithm.

results.notes: Since alpha T bounds L*_T, this is a sqrt(L* K) first-order lower bound.

bound.regime: T >= max(32K, 601), alpha in [max(2 c_1 log T, 8K)/T, 1/4]

symbols.a_ball: radius alpha of the small-variation ball: Q_T/(TK) <= alpha

source.label: thm:variation-lowerbound
source.quote: Let $K \geq 2$, $T \geq (32 K) \vee 601$, and $\alpha \in [(2 c_1 \log(T) \vee 8K)/T, 1/4]$, where $c_1 = (4/9)^2 (3\sqrt{5}+1)^2 \leq 12$. Then for any randomised bandit algorithm, $\sup_{\ell_{1:T} \in \cV_{\alpha,T}} \E[\Reg_T(\ell_{1:T})] \geq \sqrt{\alpha T K} / 25$

results.notes: Equivalently Omega(sqrt(Q_T)) since Q_T <= alpha T K.

symbols.rho: bound on the per-round effective range of the losses

source.label: thm:impossibility-result-1
source.quote: Let $K \geq 2$, $T \geq 32(K-1)\log(14)$ and $\rho \geq 0.22 \sqrt{(K-1)/T}$. Then for any randomised bandit algorithm, $\sup_{\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_T \in \cC_{\rho}} \E[\Reg_T(\ell_{1:T})] \geq \sqrt{T (K-1)} / 504$

results.notes: Shows regret cannot scale with effective range rho in bandits.

source.label: thm:impossibility-result-2
source.quote: Let $K \geq 2$ and $T \geq 32(K-1)\log(14)$. Then, for any randomised bandit algorithm, there is a loss sequence $\ell_{1:T} \in [0,1]^{K T}$ such that there exists an arm $i^*$ that is optimal at every round~$t$ ..., but $\E[\Reg_T(\ell_{1:T})] \geq \sqrt{T (K-1)} / 504$

results.notes: Existence of an always-optimal arm does not improve worst-case regret.
